plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling purple rows of silvery, scented spikes stretch across the hills of Provence. The air hums with bees and smells sweet and herbal. Each slender stem carries whorls of tiny violet-blue flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak color in mid-July
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is South Africa's national flower. Its huge, artichoke-like bloom is ringed with stiff pink bracts around a soft, silky center. It flowers boldly in the cool southern winter, when many gardens are quiet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly April to October, so it covers the southern winter month of July
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient plant family. They are named after the Greek sea god Proteus, who could change his shape, because the family has so many different forms.

plants.name: Eucalyptus leucoxylon
plants.description: Pale, mottled bark gives this tree a ghostly look. In the Australian winter it is covered in fluffy flower clusters that attract flocks of honey-feeding birds. Wild trees are often cream, and many garden selections are pink or red.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through winter into spring, roughly April to September, which includes July
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, especially South Australia and Victoria
plants.funFact: Eucalyptus flowers have no petals. The fluffy 'blossom' is a mass of stamens, and a cap called an operculum covers the bud until it pops off.
